The '''Vex system''' was located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]]. It contained the [[Swamp/Legends|swampy]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Vex Major]] and the [[Vex Asteroid Belt]]. The former was [[Homeworld/Legends|home]] to a population of [[Fisher/Legends|fishers]], while the latter was inhabited by a collection of [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] [[Spacer/Legends|jocks]], [[Prospector/Legends|prospectors]], and [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Scout/Legends|scouts]]. The purpose of the original [[Colonist/Legends|colonization]] of the Vex Asteroid Belt was to explore the nearby [[Monsua Nebula/Legends|Monsua Nebula]], and the continuously unsuccessful results of the ensuing scouting runs lent the Vex [[Star system/Legends|system]] its name.

==Description==
The Vex system was a part of the [[Inner Moddell systems]] area of<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]],<ref name="EAOC" /> one of the [[Sector/Legends|subsectors]] making up the [[Inner Zuma Region]]<ref name="TEA" /> within the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Zuma sector/Legends|Zuma sector]].<ref name="EAOC" /> [[Hyperspace route/Legends|Hyperlanes]] connected it to the [[Vasha system/Legends|Vasha system]] as well as the [[Firrerre system/Legends|Firrerre system]]<ref name="TEA" /> in the [[Sugai sector/Legends|Sugai sector]].<ref name="EAOC" /> The [[Star system/Legends|system]] contained two inhabited locations: the [[Swamp/Legends|swampy]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Vex Major]] and the [[Vex Asteroid Belt]].<ref name="Endor" />

==History==
Four [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] prior to the [[Yuuzhan Vong War|Yuuzhan Vong invasion]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]],<ref name="Endor" /> which began in [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]],<ref name="TEA" /> Vex Major was [[Colonist/Legends|settled]] by a sect of the [[Order of the Ffib]], the descendants of which insisted by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the reign of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] that the planet should be called Far Gent. The Vex Asteroid Belt was colonized with the purpose of serving as a staging area for [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Scout/Legends|scouting]] runs into the nearby [[Monsua Nebula/Legends|Monsua Nebula]]. Given the particularly inhibiting [[Star/Legends|interstellar]] anomalies along that [[Nebula/Legends|nebulosity's]] fringes, however, none of those missions had been successful by the time of the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] War, which eventually led to the Vex system's unusual name.<ref name="Endor" />

==Inhabitants==
The Vex system was inhabited by [[Human/Legends|Humans]], with the population of Vex Major numbering 250,000 and the Vex Asteroid Belt having a population of three thousand. The [[Homeworld/Legends|natives]] of Vex Major were sturdy [[Fisher/Legends|fishers]] who only engaged in basic [[Merchant/Legends|trade]] with the New Republic. They were derogatorily referred to as "mudballers" by the population of the Vex Asteroid Belt, which consisted of [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] [[Spacer/Legends|jocks]], scouts, and [[Prospector/Legends|prospectors]] and was in turn known as the [[Belters (Vex Asteroid Belt)|Belters]]. The inhabitants of both locations imported [[Foodstuff/Legends|foodstuffs]] from other star systems, with technology also being imported in the Vex Asteroid Belt.<ref name="Endor" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Vex system was introduced in the [[Star Wars Gamer 9|ninth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine<ref name="Endor" /> on [[February 22]], [[2002]].<ref name="GamerDate">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20020222.html|text=Starfighters Soar in Gamer #9}}</ref> Within the magazine, the star system was mentioned in the source article "[[Endor and the Moddell Sector]]" as well as the [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] adventure "[[Race for the Tessent]]," both being written for use with [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="Endor" /><ref name="Tessent">{{GamerCite|9|Race for the Tessent}}</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Vex system in grid square H-16.<ref name="TEA" />
